text:
My husband died of a heart attack at 54. We'd been married for 27 years. He loved the sea, and his wish was for his ashes to be scattered off the coast where we'd spent every summer. A friend of mine, who has used psilocybin for years, suggested I take a small dose on the day, to help me feel close to him. I trusted her and I was desperate to feel something other than numbness.

We went out on a small boat with my two adult children and my friend. I took the mushrooms about an hour before we reached the spot. It came on as we stopped the engine. The sea was very bright, sparkling in a way that was almost painful. My son opened the urn and we each scattered a handful.

As the ashes hit the water, I saw my husband. Not as a peaceful presence, which is what I'd hoped. I saw him in the water, drowning. His face was underwater, his eyes were open, he was reaching up towards me. I could see his mouth open and the bubbles coming out. I started screaming his name and leaned over the side to reach him. My children grabbed me and held me back. They thought I'd lost my mind from grief, they didn't know about the mushrooms.

Then the vision changed. The sea was full of bodies, hundreds of grey faces under the surface, all looking up. I understood that this was death, and that he was among them, and that I had thrown him there. I felt I'd killed him. I couldn't stop sobbing.

My friend tried to calm me and told my children what was happening. My daughter was furious with her. The boat ride back took 40 minutes and I lay curled in the bottom of the boat with my eyes shut, but the faces were there behind my eyelids too. When we reached the harbour I couldn't stand up. My son carried me to the car.

That day was supposed to be our goodbye. It became the worst day of my life after the day he died.

Ich war auf einem großen Konzert in einer Halle, hatte LSD genommen und stand ziemlich weit vorne. Als die Band auf die Bühne kam, hat die Menge nach vorne gedrückt. Plötzlich war ich eingeklemmt, ich konnte meine Arme nicht bewegen und kaum atmen. Neben mir ist eine Frau gestürzt, und Leute sind über sie gestolpert. Ich habe ihre Schreie gehört. Für mich hat sich die Menge in ein einziges Tier verwandelt, das mich zerquetschen will. Die Lichter haben geblitzt, die Musik war ohrenbetäubend, und ich war mir sicher, dass ich hier sterbe.

Ich weiß nicht mehr, wie ich rausgekommen bin. Irgendwann stand ich an der Seite, an einer Wand, und habe nach Luft geschnappt. Mein Shirt war zerrissen. Ich habe am ganzen Körper gezittert. Ich hatte panische Angst, dass die Frau tot ist. Ich bin raus aus der Halle und habe stundenlang draußen auf dem Parkplatz gesessen, während der Trip weiterging, und habe immer wieder ihr Gesicht gesehen. Später habe ich gelesen, dass es mehrere Verletzte gab, aber keine Toten. Das hat mich nur wenig beruhigt.

I smoked DMT at home, and my partner, who was supposed to sit for me, left the room halfway through to take a phone call. I came back to an empty room and felt totally abandoned and lost. I didn't know where I was or if I was alive. I lay there alone for maybe half an hour after the main effects wore off, crying and calling for him. When he came back he didn't understand why I was so upset.

I grew up in a very strict religious family. By my twenties I'd left the church, but a lot of the beliefs were still in me somewhere, I just didn't know it. I took LSD with a couple of friends at my apartment. It was my third time.

About two hours in, I started to feel something inside my chest. A presence. At first it felt like warmth, then it turned cold and heavy. I suddenly 'knew' that this was a demon, that by taking drugs I had opened a door, and that the demon had come in. Every warning my mother had ever given me came rushing back. I felt it moving inside me, taking over my arms, my voice. When I tried to speak it came out in a deep, strange voice, or that's how it sounded to me. My friends were scared, which made me more convinced that they could see the demon too.

I started praying, out loud, the old prayers from my childhood. I hadn't said them in years. I begged God to forgive me. I felt the demon laughing inside me. I saw its face in the mirror instead of mine, grey and twisted. I scratched at my arms trying to get it out, I drew blood. My friends tried to stop me and I fought them off.

One of my friends, in a panic, called my mother because he didn't know what else to do. That was a mistake, though I understand why he did it. My mother and father arrived about an hour later with the pastor from their church. They saw me bleeding and screaming and praying, and they believed exactly what I believed. The pastor put his hands on my head and started a deliverance prayer, which is like an exorcism. My parents held my arms. They were shouting at the demon to leave me, commanding it in the name of Jesus. This went on for a long time, at least an hour. I was terrified, I was in agony, and I was being held down by my parents while a man shouted at the thing inside me.

At some point I collapsed and they took that as the demon leaving. My mother cried and hugged me and said I was saved. I was still tripping and still felt the presence, just weaker. They took me home with them and I spent the next three days at my parents' house, being prayed over, made to read scripture, not allowed to be alone. I didn't know how to tell them it was the drug. I wasn't sure myself.

Eventually I went back to my apartment. My friends were shaken and we never talked about it properly. I didn't tell my parents about the LSD until two years later.

Ich hatte auf einer Party Ketamin genommen und bin auf dem Weg zur Toilette die Treppe hinuntergestürzt. Ich habe mir den Kopf aufgeschlagen und überall war Blut. Durch das Ketamin habe ich keinen Schmerz gespürt, aber ich hatte das Gefühl, dass mein Körper nicht mehr zu mir gehört und dass ich gleich sterbe. Ich habe die Leute um mich herum gesehen, die geschrien haben, aber ich war wie in einer anderen Welt, weit weg. Im Krankenwagen hatte ich das Gefühl, ich schwebe über meinem Körper. Im Krankenhaus wurde die Wunde genäht, und ich hatte eine leichte Gehirnerschütterung. Ich habe mich sehr geschämt, als ich wieder klar war.

I bought 'microdose gummies' from an online shop that claimed they were mushroom-based. Turns out they contained Amanita muscaria, which I found out later. I took two because I didn't feel anything from one. A couple of hours later I started feeling very drunk and confused. I couldn't walk straight, my muscles were twitching, and I kept falling asleep and waking up in different rooms of my flat without remembering how I got there. In between, I had dream-like visions, my grandmother talking to me, a dog made of smoke. I lost track of what was dream and what was real. At one point I woke up on the balcony in my underwear in the cold and didn't know how long I'd been there. I was terrified I'd done something in my sleep, like walk out onto the street. It went on all night. I threw up several times. In the morning I was completely exhausted and had a terrible headache. I couldn't remember large chunks of the night. I was scared that I had poisoned myself permanently.

I was 16 and on a school trip abroad with my class. One of my classmates had bought LSD from someone in the hostel and a few of us took it in our room in the evening. I'd never taken anything before. For a while it was funny, then it got very intense. I couldn't stop seeing patterns on everyone's faces and I started feeling like the room was full of people watching us.

Then a teacher knocked on the door for the evening check. Everyone panicked. Two of the boys tried to act normal but I couldn't. I was sitting on my bed staring at the wall and when the teacher asked me a question I just started crying. She realised something was wrong and called the head teacher. They separated us and questioned us one by one. The head teacher was very angry and said they'd have to inform our parents and the police in the country we were in.

I was taken to a local hospital in a taxi with a teacher. I didn't speak the language. The doctors were rough and impatient. They took blood and I thought they were going to experiment on me. I was crying and asking for my mum. The teacher sat next to me with a cold face. I felt like a criminal.

The next day I was sent home early on a plane with a teacher escort. My parents met me at the airport. The silence in the car home was the worst feeling ever.

Nach einer schmerzhaften Trennung wollte ich mit Pilzen allein im Wald eine Art Heilungsreise machen. Ich hatte meinen Hund dabei, einen jungen Mischling, den ich nach der Trennung behalten hatte. Er war für mich das Wichtigste in dieser Zeit. Ich nahm etwa 3 Gramm und setzte mich mit ihm auf eine Lichtung.

Am Anfang war es schön. Die Bäume leuchteten, ich habe viel geweint und mich mit dem Hund verbunden gefühlt. Dann, auf dem Höhepunkt, ist er plötzlich einem Reh hinterhergerannt. Ich habe ihn gerufen, aber er kam nicht zurück. Ich wollte ihm nachlaufen, aber ich konnte kaum stehen, der Waldboden bewegte sich unter meinen Füßen wie Wasser. Ich bin hingefallen und habe gerufen und geschrien, immer wieder seinen Namen.

Ich habe mich auf die Suche gemacht und bin durch den Wald gestolpert. Es wurde langsam dunkel. Jeder Schatten war für mich ein Hund, und dann wieder nicht. Ich hörte ihn bellen, aus allen Richtungen gleichzeitig. Ich war mir sicher, dass er tot ist und dass es meine Schuld ist, weil ich ihn nicht an die Leine genommen habe. Ich hatte das Gefühl, alles zu verlieren, was ich liebe, zuerst meine Beziehung und jetzt ihn.

Irgendwann kam ich an eine Landstraße. Und da lag er. Ein Auto hatte ihn angefahren, und der Fahrer war weitergefahren. Er lebte noch, aber er war schwer verletzt. Ich weiß nicht, wie ich es geschafft habe, aber ich habe ihn auf den Arm genommen und bin die Straße entlanggelaufen, bis ein Auto angehalten hat. Die Frau hat uns zu einem Tiernotdienst gefahren. Auf der Fahrt habe ich die ganze Zeit sein Blut an meinen Händen gesehen, und die Farben sind explodiert, und ich dachte, ich verliere den Verstand.

Er ist in der Nacht gestorben. Ich war noch nicht ganz nüchtern, als mir die Tierärztin das gesagt hat. Ich habe sie angeschrien und dann nur noch geweint. Die Frau, die uns gefahren hat, hat mich nach Hause gebracht. Ich weiß bis heute nicht ihren Namen.
Mushrooms and weed at a friend's flat. I felt my heart stop, then start, then stop. I threw up and cried for hours thinking I was dying.

My younger brother is autistic, he was 19 at the time. He'd heard me talk about LSD and really wanted to try it, and I agreed, thinking I'd look after him. We took a small dose in my flat. For me it was mild, but he reacted very strongly. He became overwhelmed by the sounds and lights, started hitting his head and screaming, and didn't respond to me at all. I tried everything, dimming the lights, putting on his favourite music, holding him the way our mum does. Nothing worked. Then I got scared too and my own trip turned dark. I felt like I was drowning in his distress and that I had destroyed my brother's mind. I called our mum, who came over. It took hours for him to calm down. She was very angry with me, rightly.
Viel zu hoch dosiertes LSD. Ich habe mich selbst völlig verloren und dachte, ich bin für immer verrückt.

This is embarrassing. I met a guy on a dating app and on our second date he suggested we take mushrooms at his place. I liked him and wanted to seem adventurous, so I said yes. He gave me what he said was a 'normal' amount.

About an hour in, I started to feel very unsafe. His flat was unfamiliar and dark and there were strange art prints on the walls that started moving. I looked at him and suddenly didn't know him at all, he was a stranger, and I was alone in a stranger's apartment, high, with no way to leave because I couldn't think straight enough to order a taxi. I became convinced he'd planned this to take advantage of me. He was actually being quite nice, offering me water and asking if I was okay, but every kind gesture seemed like manipulation.

Then he said he needed to go out to get something from a friend, and he left. I was alone in his flat for what was probably 20 minutes but felt like a whole night. I hid in the bathroom. I heard noises from the neighbours and thought it was people coming for me. I called my best friend but couldn't explain where I was. When he came back, I was crying in the bathroom and he looked annoyed. He called me a taxi eventually. I sat in the back of the taxi feeling the whole city crushing in on me.
